posts.engagement_rate_source: LinkedIn's own 'Post performance' panel (Page posts -> Preview results -> Show all results), not manually recomputed -- their formula is authoritative and may weight fields (e.g. clicks) differently than a naive reactions+comments+shares/impressions calc.
posts.notes: DRY RUN reading, not a real nightly check. First post from the pipeline, ad hoc timing (not from the exploration rotation) since the timing-intelligence system didn't exist yet when this was posted -- do not count as a slot trial in timing-intelligence/state.json. Also far too immature (42 min old, 0 followers) to mean anything about slot performance; logged purely to validate the /orl-timing --log-previous mechanics work end to end.

Scheduled automation (/orl-publish --fire) failed to actually fire: found two bugs, (1) both scheduled tasks pointed at bare 'claude' which Task Scheduler couldn't resolve -- fixed to use claude.exe's full path, (2) the standalone claude.exe CLI's OAuth login had expired and could not auto-refresh, which blocked the retried run too -- needs an API key instead of OAuth for reliable unattended use (user action required, not fixed yet). Published manually instead, roughly 11 hours after the intended 00:00 slot. DO NOT mark 00:00 as tried in timing-intelligence/state.json based on this entry -- the actual post time diverged too far from the assigned slot to say anything about how 00:00 itself performs.
